claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and the child or children you're inquiring about.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're asking about your son Alex who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

**Are you responsible for Alex? By this I mean, does Alex live with you, or do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit would pay towards the cost of looking after him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum. And I'm not really in a position to contribute financially at the moment - I don't give any money towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

Just to confirm I understand correctly: Alex lives with his mother, and you don't currently contribute financially towards his care or upkeep.

**Is there any other reason why you might be considered responsible for Alex - for example, do you have any formal arrangements in place regarding his care, or does he spend significant time living with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there aren't any formal arrangements. He just lives with his mum full-time. I don't have him staying with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old and lives full-time with his mother
- You don't contribute financially towards his upkeep
- There are no formal care arrangements and he doesn't stay with you

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you must be responsible for the child. This means either the child lives with you, OR you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards the cost of looking after them.

Since Alex lives with his mother full-time and you don't contribute financially towards his care, you would not meet the responsibility requirement for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Assessment Complete**

I'm sorry, but based on your circumstances, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Why:** Child Benefit requires you to be responsible for the child, which means either:
1. The child lives with you, OR
2. You contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards their care

Since Alex lives with his mother full-time and you don't currently contribute financially to his upkeep, you don't meet the responsibility requirement.

**Note:** Alex's mother may be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him if she meets the eligibility criteria, as she is the one responsible for his care.

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Alex comes to live with you or you start contributing regularly to his care), you may wish to reassess your eligibility at that time.
